title: Guided onboarding checklist: step copy + microcopy (titles, descriptions, CTAs, error states, tone)
creator: Tessa Morgan
project: Guided onboarding + first production launch checklist (Hosted API)
content:
Context
- This ticket defines the end-user copy for the Console guided onboarding checklist (Phase 1: Hosted API, self-serve) and establishes tone/microcopy rules so Console + docs + quickstarts stay consistent.
- Copy must support a progressive checklist with (1) clear next action, (2) predictable validation expectations, and (3) confidence-building production guidance.
- This copy is referenced by:
  - Console UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-guided-onboarding-ux-spec-2026-01.json
  - PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-checklist-prd-2026-01.json
  - Docs IA mapping: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/onboarding-info-architecture-update-2026.json
  - First production launch checklist definition: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/first-production-launch-checklist.json

Goals for the copy
1) Reduce ambiguity: user should understand what success looks like for each step without reading a long doc.
2) Reduce “dead ends”: each step has a primary CTA and a fallback CTA (“Learn more”/“Troubleshoot”) where appropriate.
3) Set expectations for validation: where we can auto-detect, say so; where we can’t, be explicit.
4) Match Redwood voice: developer-first, direct, no marketing language.

Non-goals
- Copy for Dedicated/Private onboarding (follow-on).
- Full troubleshooting content (lives in docs), but we include short error-state copy and links.

Terminology decisions (must be consistent across Console + docs)
- Use “Project” to mean the entity that owns API keys / usage within an Org.
- Use “Org” only when necessary (e.g., “Org settings”). Default to “Project” in checklist text.
- Use “API key” (not “token”). If we must reference header: “Authorization: Bearer <key>”.
- Use “Test key” / “Production key” (not “dev”/“live”) to align with API key UX changes.
- Use “request” for an API call, “response” for output, and “streaming” for server-sent incremental tokens.

Tone + style guidelines
- Be concise. Front-load the verb (e.g., “Create an API key”).
- Use sentence case for titles.
- Avoid “Congratulations!” / celebratory copy in primary flow. Keep completion feedback short.
- Prefer concrete outcomes over vague goals (“Get a 200 response” > “Try the API”).
- Don’t blame the user in error states. Use “We couldn’t verify…” rather than “You didn’t…”.
- Avoid implying we read prompt content. Explicitly state we only detect request success, not prompt text.
- When referencing time, avoid hard promises; use ranges (“usually within ~1 minute”).

Checklist structure + step copy (V1)

Group label: Get set up

Step 1
- Title: Create an API key
- Description (default): Create a key to authenticate requests to the Redwood API.
- Primary CTA: Create key
- Secondary CTA: View API key docs
- Helper note (small text): Keys are scoped to this project. Keep them secret.
- Validation copy:
  - Pending: Waiting for a key to be created
  - Complete: API key created
- Error state (if key creation fails):
  - Message: We couldn’t create your key. Try again, or check your permissions.
  - CTA: Try again
  - Link: Contact support

Step 2
- Title: Install an SDK (recommended)
- Description (default): Use our Python, TypeScript, or Go SDK for retries, streaming, and typed errors.
- Primary CTA: Choose an SDK
- Secondary CTA: Use REST instead
- Option labels (inside selector): Python / TypeScript / Go
- Validation behavior note: Not auto-validated in Phase 1.
- “Mark as done” label (manual completion): I installed an SDK

Group label: Make your first request

Step 3
- Title: Send your first request
- Description (default): Make a successful API call (HTTP 200) to confirm auth and connectivity.
- Primary CTA: Copy example
- Secondary CTA: Open quickstart
- Validation copy:
  - Pending: Waiting for your first successful request
  - In progress (optional, if we detect attempts): Requests received—waiting for a successful response
  - Complete: First successful request detected
- Validation expectations (tooltip/help): We detect request success from API logs/metrics. It may take up to ~1 minute to appear.

Step 4
- Title: Stream tokens to improve UX
- Description (default): Enable streaming so users see output as it’s generated.
- Primary CTA: View streaming example
- Secondary CTA: Learn when to use streaming
- Validation copy:
  - Pending: Waiting for your first streaming response
  - Complete: Streaming session detected
- Error state (common beta issue: disconnect):
  - Title (inline): Streaming disconnected?
  - Message: If the connection closes early, add a read timeout and retry on network errors.
  - CTA: Troubleshoot streaming

Group label: Production basics

Step 5
- Title: Add timeouts and retries
- Description (default): Set timeouts and retry on transient errors to reduce user-visible failures.
- Primary CTA: See retry guidance
- Secondary CTA: Error codes reference
- Manual completion label: I added timeouts and retries
- Notes:
  - This is intentionally separate from “First production launch” so teams hit reliability basics early (per Support feedback: 408/streaming drop-offs were common).

Step 6
- Title: Understand rate limits and quotas
- Description (default): Learn what triggers 429s and how to back off safely.
- Primary CTA: View quota details
- Secondary CTA: Handling 429s
- Validation behavior: Manual completion for Phase 1 (we can track link click, but do not treat it as “understood”).
- Optional inline hint: If you’re seeing 429s during onboarding, reduce concurrency or request a higher quota.

Step 7
- Title: Check usage and costs
- Description (default): Use the Usage dashboard to see tokens, latency, and error rates.
- Primary CTA: Open Usage dashboard
- Secondary CTA: Export usage data
- Validation copy:
  - Pending: Waiting for a Usage dashboard visit
  - Complete: Usage dashboard visited
- Microcopy under title (small): Tip: Filter by model and time range to debug spikes.

Group label: First production launch

Step 8
- Title: Create a production API key
- Description (default): Use a production key in your deployed environment. Keep test keys for local development.
- Primary CTA: Create production key
- Secondary CTA: Key safety tips
- Validation copy:
  - Pending: Waiting for a production key
  - Complete: Production key created
- Error prevention callout (shown if a user has only test keys and is hitting 401/403):
  - Title: Using a test key in production?
  - Message: Test keys may be restricted. Create a production key for deployed apps.
  - CTA: Create production key

Step 9
- Title: Set up basic monitoring
- Description (default): Monitor errors and latency so you can catch issues before users do.
- Primary CTA: Monitoring guide
- Secondary CTA: Webhooks / tracing
- Manual completion label: I set up monitoring

Step 10 (final)
- Title: Launch with a rollback plan
- Description (default): Roll out safely (canary or staged) and know how you’ll revert if quality or latency regresses.
- Primary CTA: First production launch checklist
- Secondary CTA: Rollout best practices
- Completion state:
  - Complete title: Ready to launch
  - Complete description: You’ve completed the recommended basics for your first production launch.

Step state microcopy (global)
- Not started: Not started
- In progress: In progress
- Complete: Complete
- Blocked (if we add later): Blocked

Checklist empty state (new user landing)
- Header: Get to your first production launch
- Body: Follow these steps to make your first successful request, understand limits, and ship safely.
- Primary CTA: Start checklist
- Secondary CTA: Skip for now

Checklist “resume” state (returning user)
- Header: Continue onboarding
- Body: You’re {N} steps from your first production launch.
- CTA: Continue

Validation delay microcopy (where applicable)
- Inline: Just made a request? This step may take up to ~1 minute to update.
- Link: Refresh

Common error-state copy (reusable patterns)

1) Unable to verify completion (generic)
- Title: We couldn’t verify this step
- Message: Try again in a minute. If it still doesn’t update, you can continue—this won’t block API usage.
- CTAs: Refresh / View troubleshooting

2) 401 unauthorized (frequent onboarding failure)
- Title: Getting a 401?
- Message: Check that you’re using the correct API key for this project and that it’s active.
- CTAs: Manage API keys / Troubleshoot 401

3) 429 rate limited
- Title: Getting a 429?
- Message: You’re sending requests faster than your current quota allows. Back off and retry with jitter.
- CTAs: View quotas / Handling 429s

4) CORS / browser issues (if we surface)
- Title: Calling the API from a browser?
- Message: For security, we recommend calling Redwood from your backend. If you must call from a browser, review CORS guidance.
- CTAs: Recommended architecture / CORS troubleshooting

CTA conventions
- Use verb + object: “Create key”, “Open quickstart”, “View streaming example”.
- Avoid “Learn more” as a primary CTA unless no action is possible.
- When linking out to docs, CTA should name what’s behind the link (e.g., “Troubleshoot 401”, not “Docs”).

Accessibility / UI constraints (notes for implementation)
- Titles must fit in one line at 320px width when possible; if wrapping, no more than 2 lines.
- Avoid inline code blocks in titles. Inline code is OK in descriptions (e.g., “HTTP 200”).
- Error states should be screen-reader friendly: start with a short title, then actionable message.

Open questions (resolved in this ticket)
- Q: Should we include a separate “retries/timeouts” step, or bundle into production launch?
  - Decision: Separate step (Step 5) based on Support feedback + beta interview notes. Production grouping still references it.
- Q: Should “rate limits/quotas” be an auto-validated step?
  - Decision: Manual completion for Phase 1; track clicks for analytics but do not mark complete based on click.
- Q: Should we use “workspace” vs “org” terminology?
  - Decision: “Org” internally, but “Project” in most copy; mention Org only in settings.

Acceptance criteria
- Copy is implemented in Console checklist UI and matches step order in the UX spec.
- Step titles/descriptions are consistent with docs IA and deep-link destinations.
- Support reviewed error-state phrasing for 401/429/streaming disconnect and confirmed it won’t create false promises.
- PM (Nikhil/Marissa) signed off on step naming and production language.

References
- UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-guided-onboarding-ux-spec-2026-01.json
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-checklist-prd-2026-01.json
- First production launch checklist (internal): sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/first-production-launch-checklist.json
- Support known failures doc (for error-state alignment): sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/onboarding-common-failures-and-fixes.json
comments: 2026-01-10 (Kenji Nakamura): Drafted V1 step titles + descriptions. Added explicit validation-delay copy to reduce confusion when steps don’t update immediately.
2026-01-14 (Priya Shah): +1 to separating retries/timeouts from prod launch. Biggest early pain is streaming disconnects and 401s from wrong key; please make those error states very direct.
2026-01-18 (Marissa Cole): Requested we avoid marking quotas/rate-limits as complete on doc-click. OK to track click for funnel, but completion should remain manual for now.
2026-02-05 (Elliot Price): Confirmed terminology alignment: “Project” should be default. Also requested doc-link CTAs be specific (e.g., “Troubleshoot 401”) to reduce bounce. Incorporating.
2026-02-12 (Tessa Morgan): Approved final copy set for beta. Follow-up: once telemetry validates step lag, we may adjust the “~1 minute” wording to avoid false precision.
